subtopics.title: The Four Factors and the Four Rewards

questions.question: Which pairing of factor and remuneration is completely correct?
options: Natural resources — rent; labour — wages and salaries; capital — interest; entrepreneurship — profit
Natural resources — profit; labour — rent; capital — wages; entrepreneurship — interest
Natural resources — interest; labour — profit; capital — rent; entrepreneurship — wages
All four factors are rewarded with dividends

questions.question: In economics, capital means:
options: The money in a business bank account
REAL capital — the man-made means of production such as machinery, buildings and vehicles, which were produced in order to produce further goods
Shares listed on the stock exchange
The owner's personal savings

questions.question: Households and firms meet in the FACTOR market when:
options: Firms sell finished goods to households
Government collects tax from firms
Households supply land, labour, capital and enterprise, and firms pay rent, wages, interest and profit for them
Banks lend to households

questions.question: Why are dividends NOT a factor remuneration?
options: Because they are illegal in South Africa
Because only government may pay them
Because they are the same thing as interest
Because they are profit being distributed to shareholders after that profit has already been earned as the reward to entrepreneurship

subtopics.title: Natural Resources and Labour Under the Microscope

questions.question: Rent on a well-placed Durban shop site is high mainly because:
options: The total supply of that site is FIXED, so its price is determined almost entirely by demand
It cost a great deal to manufacture the site
The municipality sets the rent by law
Building costs have risen

questions.question: Labour is described as PERISHABLE because:
options: Workers become ill easily
A day of labour not worked is lost permanently — it cannot be stored, which is why unemployment is a pure loss rather than a postponement
Wages fall over time
Skills always decline

questions.question: Under the Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Act, mineral rights in South Africa:
options: Belong to the surface landowner
Belong to the mining company that finds them
Vest in the STATE, with companies holding rights by licence
Belong to the municipality

questions.question: High unemployment existing alongside a shortage of high-level skills is best described as:
options: A shortage of jobs only
A fall in the labour force
A rise in productivity
A skills MISMATCH — the skills supplied are not the skills demanded

questions.question: The Gqeberha firm has sales of R4 000 000 and buys in R1 500 000 of steel, electricity and services. Its VALUE ADDED is:
Wages R1 600 000, rent R240 000, interest R160 000 and depreciation R200 000 come out of value added of R2 500 000. Profit is therefore:
Profit is called a RESIDUAL because:
options: It is always small
It is paid before wages
It is whatever remains after the contractual payments to the other factors, and it can be negative
It is fixed by contract at the start of the year

questions.question: The R1 500 000 of bought-in steel and electricity is excluded from the factor share-out because:
options: It is a government levy
It is a capital expense
It is not a real cost
It is INTERMEDIATE consumption — it already paid wages and profits inside the supplying firms, so counting it again would be double counting

subtopics.title: Local Economic Planning, Access and Empowerment Procurement

questions.question: The Integrated Development Plan (IDP) is:
options: The plan every municipality must adopt and review annually, inside which local economic development sits
The Reserve Bank's monetary policy statement
A national tax schedule
A company's business plan submitted to SARS

questions.question: Why does a lack of secure land tenure block access to the factors of production?
options: Because farming is banned without title
Because without registered title there is no COLLATERAL, so banks will not lend and the venture never starts
Because municipalities refuse trading licences
Because land without title has no productive use

questions.question: Which list gives elements of the B-BBEE scorecard?
options: Inflation, unemployment, growth and the exchange rate
Rent, wages, interest and profit
Ownership, management control, skills development, enterprise and supplier development, and socio-economic development
Primary, secondary and tertiary sectors

questions.question: Under the Preferential Procurement Policy Framework Act, the 80/20 and 90/10 systems mean that:
options: Only 20 per cent of tenders may be awarded
Government pays 90 per cent of the price
Tenders are drawn by lottery
Most points are awarded for price and a fixed remainder for specific goals such as transformation, with 90/10 applied to larger contracts

subtopics.title: The Rank, the Driver, the Kombi and the Owner

questions.question: In the taxi business, the kombi, tyres and card machine are:
options: CAPITAL — things people built in order to earn with, whose funding costs interest
Natural resources
Labour
Entrepreneurship

questions.question: The person who spotted the route, borrowed for the kombi, hires the driver and carries the loss when the gearbox goes is supplying:
options: Labour, and earns a wage
ENTREPRENEURSHIP, and earns profit
Capital, and earns interest
Natural resources, and earns rent

questions.question: "Money is not capital" means:
options: Money has no value
Businesses should not borrow
The R400 000 in the account is not the factor of production — the kombi it buys is
Only cash counts as a factor

questions.question: The kombi takes R60 000 in fares and spends R22 500 on diesel, tyres and repairs bought from other businesses. The value it ADDED is:
Wages R18 000, rank fees R2 500, interest R4 000 and R6 000 set aside for wear come out of R37 500. The owner is left with:
The order of payment in the taxi business shows that:
options: The owner is paid first, at a guaranteed amount
Everyone else is paid FIRST at agreed amounts and the owner LAST at an amount nobody promised — which is why the owner decides
Wages are a residual
Interest is paid only if there is profit

questions.question: Why is the R22 500 of diesel and tyres left out of the taxi's value added?
options: It is a tax
It is not a real expense
It already paid a wage at the garage and a profit at the tyre factory, so counting it again would count the same money twice
It is paid in cash

subtopics.title: Whose Town Is It — Planning, Doors and Tenders

questions.question: "A district with good soil and no packhouse sends its tomatoes away raw and buys the sauce back" illustrates:
options: The purpose of local economic planning — combining a district's factors locally so the value added stays at home
The law of demand
The national minimum wage
The circular flow of money only

questions.question: The three bakers with the same idea show that access depends on:
options: The quality of the business idea alone
Collateral, information and transport — not the quality of the idea
The size of the municipality
The interest rate only

questions.question: Attending the ward meeting matters economically because:
options: Attendance is paid
It is compulsory by law for every resident
The plan is written whether you are there or not, and the road, clinic and trading stalls go where the plan says
It replaces the need for tenders

questions.question: The economic point of empowerment procurement is that:
options: It is a form of charity to small firms
It lowers the price government pays
It replaces taxation
Demand creates factor incomes — so pointing a share of the state's enormous purchasing at excluded suppliers redirects income toward them
